event.title: fix(memory): move local embeddings to llama.cpp provider
event.body:
Ignore the huge diff, this is just a proposal for @vincentkoc 

## Summary

Local memory embeddings could break because the core package no longer owns `node-llama-cpp`.
This moves the local llama.cpp embedding runtime into a real official plugin that owns that dependency.
Core now starts the provider plugin when memory search is configured for `local`, and the memory host worker imports `node-llama-cpp` from that plugin instead of assuming it exists at the root.

Fixes #88705

## What Changed

The local embedding provider is now owned by a new `@openclaw/llama-cpp-provider` plugin.
Memory core keeps the generic memory behavior, while the llama.cpp-specific dependency and setup guidance live in the provider package.

- Added `extensions/llama-cpp` with an embedding provider manifest, package metadata, shrinkwrap, tests, and docs.
- Removed the built-in `local` provider registration from `memory-core`.
- Added memory-host SDK support for passing a module import URL into the worker, so the worker imports plugin-local `node-llama-cpp`.
- Updated gateway startup plugin planning so configured memory embedding providers, including provider aliases, start their owning plugins.
- Updated `doctor memory-search` so `provider: "local"` only passes when the gateway reports the provider ready.
- Updated the official external plugin catalog, package excludes, plugin docs, and labeler ownership.

## Testing

I tested the provider boundary, memory startup planning, doctor behavior, package metadata, and type surfaces.
Autoreview was also run after implementation and came back clean.

- `node scripts/generate-npm-shrinkwrap.mjs --package-dir extensions/llama-cpp --check`
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/node-llama.ts packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/embeddings.ts packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/embeddings-worker.ts extensions/llama-cpp/index.ts extensions/llama-cpp/src/embedding-provider.ts extensions/llama-cpp/index.test.ts src/commands/doctor-memory-search.ts src/commands/doctor-memory-search.test.ts src/plugins/gateway-startup-plugin-ids.ts src/plugins/channel-plugin-ids.test.ts src/plugins/official-external-plugin-catalog.test.ts`
- `git diff --check`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/llama-cpp/index.test.ts packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/embeddings.test.ts extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-embedding-timeout.test.ts extensions/memory-core/src/memory/provider-adapter-registration.test.ts extensions/memory-core/src/memory/generic-embedding-provider.bridge.test.ts extensions/memory-core/src/memory/index.test.ts src/plugins/channel-plugin-ids.test.ts src/commands/doctor-memory-search.test.ts src/plugins/contracts/extension-runtime-dependencies.contract.test.ts src/plugins/contracts/memory-embedding-provider.contract.test.ts src/plugins/official-external-plugin-catalog.test.ts test/openclaw-npm-release-check.test.ts test/package-manager-config.test.ts test/plugin-npm-runtime-build.test.ts`
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo`
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.extensions.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/extensions.tsbuildinfo`
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/extensions-test.tsbuildinfo`
- Autoreview: clean, no accepted/actionable findings.

Not completed:

- `pnpm docs:list` did not complete locally. One run reported `[ERROR] fetch failed`; later attempts hung and were killed.

## Risks

The main risk is packaging and install behavior for the new official external plugin.
The PR keeps core plugin-agnostic and pins the llama.cpp runtime in the plugin shrinkwrap, but release validation should still prove the plugin package installs cleanly on supported platforms.

linked_issues.title: Bug: npm updates drop node-llama-cpp, breaking local memory_search after every OpenClaw update
linked_issues.body:
## Summary

After each recent npm-based OpenClaw update, local `memory_search` stops working because the `node-llama-cpp` optional dependency is no longer present under the installed OpenClaw package directory.

This has happened repeatedly on the same Linux host after OpenClaw updates. The workaround is always to manually reinstall `node-llama-cpp` into the OpenClaw package prefix and then retest `memory_search`.

## Environment

- OpenClaw before latest update: `2026.5.27`
- OpenClaw after latest update: `2026.5.28 (e932160)`
- Install kind: global npm package under `/home/openclaw/.npm-global/lib/node_modules/openclaw`
- Node.js: `v24.15.0`
- npm: `11.12.1`
- Gateway: systemd user service, loopback `127.0.0.1:18789`
- Memory provider: local embeddings
- Expected local model: `hf:ggml-org/embeddinggemma-300m-qat-q8_0-GGUF/embeddinggemma-300m-qat-Q8_0.gguf`

## Repro / observed flow

1. Update OpenClaw via npm from `2026.5.27` to `2026.5.28`.
2. Restart the gateway.
3. Run a local `memory_search` tool call.

## Actual result

`memory_search` becomes unavailable:

```text
results: []
disabled: true
unavailable: true
error: Local embeddings unavailable.
Reason: optional dependency node-llama-cpp is missing (or failed to install).
Detail: Cannot find package 'node-llama-cpp' imported from /home/openclaw/.npm-global/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist/embeddings-C9YA6RhB.js
```

`npm ls -g --depth=0 node-llama-cpp openclaw` only showed `openclaw@2026.5.28`; `node-llama-cpp` was absent.

A local post-update check also flagged the dependency as missing:

```text
Memory-Search-Abhaengigkeit
[PROBLEM] node-llama-cpp fehlt im OpenClaw-Paket; memory_search danach im Chat testen/reparieren
```

## Expected result

After an OpenClaw npm update, local `memory_search` should keep working without manually reinstalling `node-llama-cpp` into the OpenClaw package directory.

At minimum, the update flow or doctor should detect this condition and offer a direct repair step.

## Workaround that fixes it

```bash
npm install --no-save node-llama-cpp@3.18.1 --prefix /home/openclaw/.npm-global/lib/node_modules/openclaw
cd /home/openclaw/.npm-global/lib/node_modules/openclaw && node -e "import('node-llama-cpp').then(()=>console.log('ok'))"
```

After this, the same `memory_search` call succeeds again:

```text
provider: local
model: hf:ggml-org/embeddinggemma-300m-qat-q8_0-GGUF/embeddinggemma-300m-qat-Q8_0.gguf
hits: 3
```

The post-update check then passes:

```text
CLI version: 2026.5.28
Package version: 2026.5.28
Gateway version: 2026.5.28
node-llama-cpp present
OK: 8 | Hinweise: 0 | Probleme: 0
```

## Why this matters

For agents configured to rely on local/free memory search, every npm update silently removes or fails to preserve the native local embeddings dependency. The gateway can otherwise look healthy, so the breakage only appears when an agent tries to recall memory.

## Related context

This seems adjacent to local memory/provider work such as #70596 and #70873, but the issue here is specifically the npm update/install result: `node-llama-cpp` disappears from the installed OpenClaw package prefix and must be reinstalled manually after updates.
